q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The Q2 FY2027 earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 19, 2026. **Time remaining: 7 days.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has already issued forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which means the guidance range is $89.18 billion to $92.82 billion.

This guidance will be formally reissued or confirmed during the August 26 earnings call. The question asks what forward guidance NVIDIA will provide—this is essentially asking what they have already publicly committed to, with minor possibility of revision.

Key supporting evidence:
- The May 20, 2026 guidance of $91.0B ± 2% is explicitly stated in SEC filings and press releases
- Current consensus estimates are $91.85B, only 0.9% above the midpoint, suggesting the market expects NVIDIA to meet/slightly exceed guidance
- The guidance explicitly excludes Data Center compute revenue from China, a material constraint that NVIDIA has already factored in
- With only 7 days until the earnings call, major guidance revisions are uncommon unless there's been a significant unexpected development

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA **reaffirms or slightly raises its $91.0B guidance**, staying within the 89.18–92.82B range or potentially moving modestly higher if demand has exceeded expectations.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Unexpected weakness in data center orders or customer delays
- Macro deterioration or recession concerns that reduce customer capex appetite
- Stronger-than-expected competition eroding pricing or market share
- Supply chain disruptions
- Geopolitical export restrictions tightening beyond current China policy
- Significant miss on Q1 actual results (though this seems unlikely given prior guidance accuracy)

Lower guidance would likely land in the range of **$88–90B**, below the midpoint.

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Better-than-expected demand for H100/H200 GPUs and AI accelerators
- Upside surprises in enterprise and cloud customer deployments
- Stronger CPU revenue from Vera adoption than anticipated (CFO guided $20B for full FY2027)
- Market share gains vs. AMD and other competitors
- Faster ramp in new product lines
- Reversion of China exclusion (unlikely but would be material upside)

Higher guidance would likely land in the range of **$93–96B**, above the current midpoint.

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provided explicitly states NVIDIA's May 20, 2026 guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**, which translates to a midpoint of $91.0B with a ±2% range of $89.18B–$92.82B.

The current consensus estimate is **$91.85 billion**, representing a modest 0.9% premium to the midpoint.

NVIDIA's historical track record shows they tend to issue achievable guidance and often beat it. They are conservative in their guidance methodology.

---

## Probability Distribution

Given:
- The explicit May 2026 guidance of $91.0B ± 2%
- Current consensus at $91.85B (0.9% above midpoint)
- 7 days until earnings (very short timeframe for major guidance revision)
- NVIDIA's historical conservative guidance practice

The distribution should be centered around **$91–92B** with meaningful probability mass across the $89–94B range, and declining probability for values significantly outside this band.

**Low (10th percentile):** 89000000000
**Median (50th percentile):** 91500000000
**High (90th percentile):** 94000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's guidance issued on May 20, 2026, projected revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, explicitly excluding any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance was above the average analyst estimate of $86.84 billion at the time [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Current consensus estimates for Q2 FY2027 revenue are around $91.85 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/), [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors/), a slight premium (0.9%) over NVIDIA's midpoint guidance [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). For the upcoming Q3 FY2027 (October quarter), the consensus revenue forecast is $103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). NVIDIA's CFO, Colette Kress, anticipates $20 billion in total CPU revenue for fiscal year 2027, driven by the new Vera CPU [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).
